analysis.title: Viewpoint: Conditions Are Building For A Year End Rally
key_insights: CIO says conditions for a year-end equity rally are building. A below-the-surface correction in which a majority of S&P 500 stocks fell about 15% to 20% from their peaks appears exhausted.

The CIO attributes the risk-off period to several concerns arriving together: expectations of Fed hikes instead of cuts, oil and diesel back near 2026 highs, midterm elections, and concerns about capital availability for the AI buildout.
Market valuation has fallen to about 18x forward earnings from 22x at the start of the year. The CIO reads this as a positioning rotation out of over-crowded AI-buildout beneficiaries.
The CIO expects the risk-off period to end once Q4 guidance, FY2027 outlooks and the midterms pass. It expects focus to return to solid growth, record margins and rising productivity.

No tactical asset allocation changes this month. The CIO stays overweight Equities, prefers U.S. equities, is slightly overweight EM, slightly underweight International Developed, and slightly underweight Fixed Income overall to fund the equity overweight.

The CIO calls recent drops in Financials, parts of Industrials, higher-quality semiconductors and power-generation stocks overdone. It would use weakness to rebalance. It also says Defense looks attractively valued again and Healthcare is emerging as an AI-adoption leader.
On fixed income, the 10-year Treasury yield is near 5% with real yields above 2.5%. The CIO favors moving out of cash and the front end of the curve and extending duration toward strategic targets.
The 10-year yield peaked near 5.3% in early October, its highest level since 2002, then fell to just under 5% after the Fed held and AI-related stocks weakened.

The Fed held at 3.75%-4.00% in October (Chair Warsh), with two dissenters favoring another hike. Markets price two more hikes through mid-2027. BofA Global Research forecasts 25 bps hikes in December 2026 and March 2027.

S&P 500 breadth improved in October. The share of constituents above their 200-day moving average rose to 66% from 43% at the end of September. Equal-weight beat cap-weight by the widest monthly margin since 2009.

Sector stance: overweight Industrials, Financials and Healthcare. Neutral IT, Energy, Consumer Discretionary and Materials. Underweight Utilities, Communication Services, Real Estate and Consumer Staples.

Credit spreads widened in October to their widest of the year but remain historically tight. The CIO is slightly underweight IG and HY credit, and slightly underweight MBS. It favors tax-exempt munis for highly tax-sensitive investors.

In alternatives, hedge funds benefit from dispersion (Equity Hedge and Macro favored). Private credit non-traded BDCs still face redemption requests above 5% caps. Private equity deal value rose 20.9% QoQ in Q3.

The CIO says precious metals have corrected sharply from bubble peaks and the dollar is overvalued against the yen and renminbi. It says an end to Middle East hostilities would likely collapse oil prices.

sector_views.rationale: Capex budgets are growing, 100% bonus depreciation was enacted again, order backlogs are strong, and AI infrastructure plans continue. Valuation is elevated and momentum has stalled.
Tailwinds from deregulation, loan growth, NII growth and capital markets activity. Valuation is described as attractive. Private credit overhang is a risk.
Utilization is solid, biotech funding is improving, policy headwinds have eased, and valuation is attractive. The CIO has strong conviction in Large Biopharma and Small- and Mid-cap Biotech.
Elevated valuations, crowded positioning and margin risks offset strong earnings growth and AI-driven flows. Near-term concerns on capex funding.
Muted outlook after strong YTD performance and uncertainty over the Middle East conflict, now in its ninth month.
Fading tax tailwinds and higher energy costs against a solid job market. The three largest companies are about 60% of the sector.
Improved pricing and demand for commodities, offset by longer-term overcapacity concerns.
Policy and affordability concerns, local resistance to data centers, and rising interest rates. Exposure was reduced in September.
Weaker operating cash flow and FCF amid aggressive capital spending increases.
Downward pressure on rental rates as leases roll, and supply-demand imbalances.
Tariffs, higher input costs, consumer trade-down to private label, and premium valuations.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 is on track for an eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit y/y EPS growth for Q3 (per the report, FactSet cited for sector growth).
All 11 S&P 500 sectors are expected to see earnings growth accelerate for full-year 2026 (FactSet, as cited in the report).
BofA Global Earnings Revision Ratio was 1.01 in October, above the 1.00 threshold where upgrades outnumber downgrades. Technology revisions improved despite AI stock weakness.
Double-digit S&P 500 earnings growth is expected in 2026 and 2027.
The 2026 EPS scenario grid for the S&P 500 runs from $335 to $395 against forward P/E of 19x to 23x. These are illustrative scenarios, not price targets.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Growth is resilient on business investment, consumer spending and government spending.
Hawkish hold with two dissenters favoring a hike.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fed funds rate, end of period (BofA Global Research)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Implies two further 25 bps hikes, in December 2026 and March 2027.
Above-average growth as the economy shifts toward midcycle.
Solid but uneven global growth, with an AI-driven export boom in Taiwan and Korea.
The CIO says inflation has likely peaked.

macro_indicators.indicator: Core CPI inflation y/y (BofA Global Research)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Core stays above the Fed's 2% target.
Peak was the highest since 2002. The CIO sees 5%+ yields as attractive and demand as strong.

risk_factors: Protracted Middle East conflict and higher-for-longer oil prices hurting earnings, inflation and capex.
Escalation of AI concerns from an earnings miss, supply shock or tighter credit conditions.
Sharper rises in U.S. interest rates, sticky inflation and the Fed response.
Releveraging by Technology and hyperscalers, and weak lower-quality HY and leveraged loans.
Private credit redemption pressure and software exposure.
Heavy new issuance pressuring credit spreads.
vol_and_positioning: Short-term positioning looks increasingly cautious, with greater downside mitigation and AI bearishness at 2026 highs, in the CIO's view.
BofA Bull & Bear Indicator is neutral at 7.1, below its 8.0 contrarian sell threshold. Global Fund Manager Survey cash is 3.9%, below the 4.0% contrarian sell threshold.
AAII survey showed bears outnumbering bulls, though sentiment is not at extreme pessimism.
S&P 500 fell below its 50- and 100-day moving averages in late October but holds above its 200-day.
Interest rate volatility rose back toward levels last seen during the March geopolitical shock.
Equity Hedge managers added shorts and later cut longs in October. TMT and Asia-focused managers gave back gains in the AI unwind.
geopolitical: U.S./Iran conflict and the Middle East conflict, now in its ninth month, with damage to energy infrastructure that will take time to fix.
A U.S.-Iran diplomatic agreement could lower energy prices and moderate inflation.
Midterm elections: the report refers to a Democratic sweep of Congress, with policy gridlock seen as historically supportive for markets.
Geopolitical risks are expected to dissipate in early 2027.
Tariff refunds are cited as support for companies, and global protectionism is cited as a risk.

tension_points.theme: AI buildout funding and equity rally
tension_points.bull_case: The CIO says EPS strength, 5%+ yield demand capping rate spikes, easing excess momentum and visible stock-level stories below the index will refocus the market on growth, margins and productivity into year-end.
tension_points.bear_case: The CIO lists escalation of AI concerns from an earnings miss, supply shock or tighter credit, plus higher oil, Fed hikes and sharper rate rises, as risks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An earnings miss, supply shock or tighter credit conditions escalating AI concerns, or sharper moves higher in U.S. rates.

theme_stances.key_argument: The below-the-surface correction appears exhausted, and focus should shift to solid growth, record margins and productivity.
theme_stances.evidence: We believe the conditions for a year-end rally in Equities are just beginning

theme_stances.key_argument: With 10-year yields near 5% and real yields above 2.5%, all-in yields are compelling and investors should move out of cash and the front end.
theme_stances.evidence: move out of cash and the front end of the curve and extend duration
